title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District
area: South-central Wisconsin, including Madison and surrounding Dane County.

context.text: No candidate filed for the Republican primary in this district. Incumbent Mark Pocan (D) defeated Douglas Alexander in the Democratic primary and is unopposed on the November 3 general election ballot.

candidates.name: Mark Pocan
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Douglas Alexander in the Democratic primary; unopposed in the general election.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District (since 2013)

summary.text: Mark Pocan is the Democratic incumbent representing Wisconsin's 2nd District since 2013. A former state legislator and small-business owner, he serves on the House Appropriations Committee and co-chairs the Congressional LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus.

background.text: Born in Kenosha, Wisconsin, in 1964; earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1986.
Previously owned Budget Signs & Specialties, a printing business.
Served on the Dane County Board of Supervisors from 1991 to 1996, and in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 1998 to 2013.

priorities.text: Says he is committed to investing in education to give future generations the tools to become leaders.
Says the budget should strengthen Social Security and Medicare and invest in job growth through infrastructure, education, and research while reducing deficits.
Says he opposes discrimination in all forms and has fought as co-chair of the Congressional LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus to end it.

positions.summary: Says he believes the country must continue to expand and innovate within the healthcare system to provide all Wisconsinites access to health insurance that meets their needs.
Says making the country more energy efficient will reduce the carbon footprint and position the U.S. to thrive in a twenty-first-century economy.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Financial Services and General Government and Labor-HHS-Education subcommittees, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Co-chairs the Congressional LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus.
